stick_finite_field_the_weil_riemann_hypo.question: Finite field - the Weil Riemann hypothesis
references: A. Weil, Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields (1940s)
P. Deligne, La conjecture de Weil I (1974) - the general case
the Hasse bound |a| <= 2 sqrt(q) for elliptic curves
stick_finite_field_the_weil_riemann_hypo.statement: For a smooth projective curve over F_q, the zeta function's reciprocal roots (Frobenius eigenvalues) satisfy |alpha| = sqrt(q) exactly. Equivalently the zeros lie on Re(s) = 1/2. This is proven - the Riemann hypothesis over finite fields is a theorem, not a conjecture.

ticks.claim: [the classical gap - restated for precision, 2026-11-25] The note that names the classical gap says 'This does NOT prove the classical RH' - still true: the Weil conjectures are a theorem about varieties over finite fields. But the gap it names is now closed by another route: the Riemann hypothesis is proved - a machine-checked Lean proof (Alpöge, 2026-11-20); no human-readable proof yet. Whether that route supplies a cohomology for the integers, as the field-with-one-element program seeks, has not been read here.

stick_the_de_bruijn_newman_constant.question: The de Bruijn-Newman constant
references: C. M. Newman (1976): Lambda exists and is real; conjecture Lambda >= 0
B. Rodgers & T. Tao (2020, Duke Math. J.): Lambda >= 0, proved
stick_the_de_bruijn_newman_constant.statement: There is a real constant Lambda such that the heat-flow deformation H_t of the Riemann xi-function has only real zeros exactly when t >= Lambda. The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to Lambda <= 0; since Lambda >= 0 is now proved, RH is equivalent to Lambda = 0.

ticks.claim: Lambda = 0: it FOLLOWS from the Riemann hypothesis, proved - a machine-checked Lean proof (Alpöge, 2026-11-20); no human-readable proof yet. The chain: the Riemann hypothesis gives Lambda <= 0 (de Bruijn 1950: once H_t has only real zeros, so does every H_s with s > t; Newman 1976 named the threshold Lambda), and Rodgers and Tao (2020) proved Lambda >= 0. Neither of those steps is new; the new link is the Riemann hypothesis. The engine re-derived none of it: the window this stick sealed stands, and its upper end now meets the lower.
ticks.source: N. G. de Bruijn, Duke Math. J. 17 (1950) 197-226; C. M. Newman, Proc. AMS 61 (1976) 245-251; B. Rodgers, T. Tao, Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6; L. Alpöge, Lean proof of RH (2026-11-20)

ticks.claim: [the one unfired mark - restated for precision, 2026-11-25] The note that names RH as Lambda = 0 says 'Lambda=0 marked open' and 'we do not claim Lambda = 0'. Both were right when minted. Since 2026-11-20 the Riemann hypothesis is proved - a machine-checked Lean proof (Alpöge, 2026-11-20); no human-readable proof yet - so Lambda <= 0, and with Rodgers-Tao Lambda = 0: see this stick's closed mark. The claim is the chain's, cited; the engine still seals only its window.

stick_the_langlands_program.question: The Langlands program
references: R. P. Langlands, letter to A. Weil (1967)
A. Wiles, Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Ann. Math. 141 (1995) 443
C. Breuil, B. Conrad, F. Diamond, R. Taylor, J. AMS 14 (2001) 843 (modularity for all E/Q)
L. Lafforgue, Invent. Math. 147 (2002) 1 (Langlands for GL(n) over function fields)
stick_the_langlands_program.statement: Is there a grand unification of mathematics — a precise correspondence between Galois representations (number theory) and automorphic forms (harmonic analysis), with their L-functions equal? The full program is a web of conjectures, largely OPEN over number fields; specific cases are proven. The open question is the general correspondence, not the proven pillars.

ticks.claim: [the open vision - restated for precision, 2026-11-25] The note of the open vision says the geometric Langlands correspondence 'remains a web of conjectures'. That was wrong when it was minted: Gaitsgory, Raskin and seven coauthors proved the unramified geometric Langlands conjecture for curves over a field of characteristic zero in five papers posted in 2024 (arXiv:2405.03599, 2405.03648, 2409.07051, 2409.08670, 2409.09856), about 800 pages; whether a journal has published them has not been read here. The arithmetic program over number fields - functoriality, the automorphy of arbitrary Galois representations - stays open. By Tao's account (2026-11-20) the machine-checked proof of the Riemann hypothesis draws on the Langlands program.
